chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Nadr ibn Shu'ayb from Yunus ibn Imran ibn Maysam from Sama'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: He said to me, 'What is wrong with you that you do not perform Hajj this year?' I said, 'There were business dealings between me and some people, and I had affairs, and perhaps that would be better (for me later).' He said, 'No, by Allah, Allah will not do good for you in that.' Then he said, 'A servant is not withheld from this House except because of a sin, and He pardons most of it.'
ai.seo_question: Why is a person prevented from performing Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) corrects the narrator’s assumption that worldly duties constitute a valid excuse for delaying Hajj, asserting instead that such hindrance is a divine consequence of sin. While God’s mercy is vast and He pardons most transgressions, the specific obstruction from fulfilling this pillar serves as a spiritual diagnostic of one's state. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on Hajj as a primary obligation that should not be deferred without compelling necessity, linking physical inability or delay to spiritual impediments.
